correctness.rationale: Exact ratio recursion is strictly increasing; Jensen and unequal variances force one negative interval. Beta-mixture CLTs and uniform CDF convergence over intervals give exact critical Gaussian TV; a wider beta-fluctuation scale yields distance one. The small-ratio global L1 expansion uses beta fourth moments, uniform summed third binomial derivatives and a binomial central limit with uniform integrability to obtain the exact phi(1) coefficient. A fresh standard-library script checks 200 rational cases plus 24 numerical convergence configurations, without treating finite checks as a proof.

originality.rationale: Distinct from the most relevant inspected primary results: prior convex order and Gaussian process approximations do not give the sharp urn-versus-binomial total-variation phase function; published Stein bounds only give \(O(n/A)\), and fixed-n pointwise corrections do not justify n→∞. value.rationale: Binary Pólya counts are a canonical reinforced alternative to independent binomial sampling; the precise regime at which the binomial approximation ceases to be accurate is needed for model approximation and distinguishability. Unlike a generic upper bound or weak CLT, the three-regime result gives the exact distance at the critical initial-mass scale and a universal small-reinforcement error constant, plus an exact finite-sample optimizing event. These constitute a coherent quantitative answer to a natural distributional approximation question, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
